# P34.13 — Chrome, format and accessibility quick fixes

**Requirement ids:** none named by the plan row; the rules applied are plan
§5.1 (**TS-03**, **TS-10**, **TS-12**) and G2 §6's claim rules ·
**Findings closed:** **QW-11**, **QW-13**, **K14 NEW-7**, **K14 NEW-8**,
**K12b NEW-11** (F-17) · findings touched: RI-49, RI-51, RI-52, RI-15,
DR-C4-14, F-189 (partial — the N-7 notice ships; the terms *content* fix
stays P34.25/P34.46's) ·
**Base:** `r11/P34.12-research-queue-truth-fixes` (chain tip — merge after
it) ·
**Ticket:**
`docs/tickets/215_P34.13__chrome-format-accessibility-quick-fixes.md`
(manifest row 215 — Round 11 / P34, sub-round 11A) ·
**Live stage:** **none** — code + copy + tests only; the public effect rides
P34.17's republish #1 under its own verbatim go.
`live_verification=false`.

## Why

The frame leaked errors and mis-shaped copy: a missing page rendered a bare
nginx 404 with no shell and no way home; there was no 403 or 410 page at all
(a corrected page just vanished); no favicon; no sitemap; every page shipped
one identical meta description; `/terms` did not resolve on the site origin
even though `robots.txt` has pointed there since launch. On the
accessibility side the wordmark's accessible name (`SIG — home`) did not
contain its visible text — a WCAG 2.5.3 label-in-name breach; a dossier
carried two landmarks both named "How we know this" (RI-49); the standalone
print dossier had no `main` landmark; and long identifiers (digests,
ruleset ids, permalinks) forced 800-px overflow at 320-px reflow (DR-C4-14).
In the text itself, Astro's tag-boundary whitespace collapsing glued words
at inline-element boundaries (`toggled):Field of view`), every count of
five or more digits rendered ungrouped, and the freshness table's "stale"
and "volatility" sort links were no-op affordances — each produced the
identical alphabetical table while claiming to sort.

## What this does

1. **Branded error pages (QW-11).** `web/src/pages/404.astro` (emitted as
   `/404.html`, matching the nginx `error_page 404` convention already in
   `ops/web/nginx.conf`), `403.astro` and `410.astro`. Each renders the real
   shell — wordmark, primary nav, skip link — with `chrome="minimal"` (no
   provenance/citation module: there is nothing on an error page to cite)
   and `noindex` (an error page is never canonical content). The 410 body
   is notice string **N-6** verbatim (`data-notice="N-6"` — B-2's notice
   allowance until GATE-G4). The `sigChrome` build integration copies the
   `/403/` and `/410/` trees to flat `403.html`/`410.html` beside
   `404.html`, so the P34.40 `error_page` wiring has files to point at.
   **Serving is recorded owed:** the nginx `error_page` change itself is
   P34.40's dark roll — `D-P34.13-1` (cites BL-084), owner P34.40.
2. **Favicon (QW-11).** `web/public/favicon.svg` — the three-letter mark on
   the shell's ink square — linked from `BaseLayout` and the print page.
3. **Canonical-only sitemap (QW-11, RI-51).** `sigChrome` walks the emitted
   pages at `astro:build:done` and writes `/sitemap.xml` listing a URL only
   when it is its *own* canonical — print pages canonicalise to their
   dossier and never appear, `noindex` pages never appear, and every URL
   sits on `https://surveillancegraph.org`. `robots.txt` gains the
   `Sitemap:` line.
4. **Unique titles and meta descriptions (QW-11).** `BaseLayout` accepts an
   optional `description`; the default is `lib/meta.ts`'s template —
   "`{title}` — Surveillance Infrastructure Graph (SIG)" — which derives a
   unique description from each page's already-unique title (copy row
   MD-01). The print page uses the same template; the freshness sort route
   gets a distinct title ("Data freshness — sorted by status", copy row
   `title`).
5. **`/terms` → the API terms (QW-11, RI-15).** `web/src/pages/terms.astro`
   links to `apiTermsUrl()` (`lib/public-api.ts` — the launch-recorded
   public base, overridable at build time via `SIG_API_BASE_URL`) with
   **N-7** verbatim beside it (`data-notice="N-7"`): the API's terms
   response is known-wrong until P34.46. It is a plain link on a noindex
   chrome page — the contract's recorded option: a meta-refresh would hide
   the notice (0-delay) or breach WCAG 2.2.1 (delayed); a true 301 is
   P34.40's nginx roll, in `D-P34.13-1`.
6. **Label-in-name + unique landmarks + print `main` + wrapped ids
   (QW-13).** The wordmark's accessible name now contains its visible text
   ("SIG Surveillance Infrastructure Graph — home", copy row WM-01).
   `HowWeKnowThis` gains a visually-hidden suffix — `— site-wide`,
   `— {pageName}`, `— this page` (copy rows HW-11…13) — so the shell module
   and the dossier's own §39.2 section no longer collide as two same-named
   regions. The standalone print document wraps its content in
   `<main id="main">`. `code`, `.sig-cite__permalink` and
   `.sig-print-footer__permalink` get `overflow-wrap/word-break:
   break-word` so digests and permalinks wrap instead of overflowing.
7. **No glued words at inline boundaries (K14 NEW-7).** Explicit `{" "}`
   separators at every tag boundary where Astro's line-wrap collapsing
   would join two words — the landing stats, dossier index, map layer
   notes, network path summaries (`Tulsa PD(preconfigured…` was real),
   citation/dispute affordances, watch/evidence/methodology/
   corrections/dispute/style-guide copy, the print toolbar/footer and the
   `data-collection` page (whose `{" "}` separators also required the
   data-collection binding test to normalise the idiom the same way the
   P34.11 batch test already did).
8. **Grouped digit runs (K14 NEW-8, §3.6).** `lib/format.ts`'s
   `groupDigits`/`fmtInt` group every run of five or more digits with
   commas — exact values, never rounded — applied at the render seam:
   landing coverage stats, the freshness table and its summary, dossier
   figure/reconciliation values. Four-digit runs (years, ISO dates) are
   untouched.
9. **No-op sort routes removed (K12b NEW-11).** The freshness `COLUMNS`
   drop `stale` and `volatility`; `getStaticPaths` (with its key list local
   to the hoisted scope) pre-renders only `source`/`status` — the two
   sorts that genuinely re-order. The stale-count and volatility columns
   still render as data; only the misleading affordance and its routes are
   gone. `REMOVED_FRESHNESS_SORT_PAGES` in the e2e registry asserts the
   routes 404; `ops/public_routes.toml` and `large-table.nojs.spec.ts`
   updated to match.
10. **Copy batch + registries (B-2).** Fifteen rows appended `pending` to
    batch-01 (NF-01/02, FB-01/02, GN-01, TR-01/02, four `title` rows,
    HW-11…13, MD-01, WM-01) with sha256s; `data-copy`/`data-notice`
    attributes bind page text to rows; the P34.11 binding test's page map
    and id prefix pattern extended for the new ids.
11. **Route allow-list.** `ops/public_routes.toml` names 404/403/410
    (routes + flat copies), `favicon.svg`, `sitemap.xml` and `terms` as
    required emits; comments keep `/task/` allow-listed for RQ-03 and note
    the `/task/` 403 → 404 mapping per G1's route table lands with the
    P34.40 wiring.

## Test plan

- `web/tests/e2e/chrome.spec.ts` (new, 11 tests) — every public page has a
  unique title AND unique meta description; `/sitemap.xml` is canonical-
  origin only, every loc resolvable and self-canonical, error/terms/print/
  internal routes absent; `robots.txt` names the sitemap; error pages
  carry the shell + home link + noindex; `/terms` carries N-7 beside an
  `https://` API-terms link and is noindex; the wordmark's accessible name
  contains its visible text; landmark names are unique on a dossier; the
  print document has exactly one `main`; no glued inline-boundary text in
  any built page (a marker-aware scan — `{" "}` separators, ` · ` spans
  and aria-hidden glyphs are not glues); no ungrouped 5+-digit run in any
  public text node (identifiers, code and permalinks excepted).
- `web/tests/unit/format.test.ts` (new) — `groupDigits`/`fmtInt` rules
  (≥5 grouped, 4 left, never rounded, ISO dates untouched);
  `apiTermsUrl` default + `SIG_API_BASE_URL` override;
  `defaultDescription` derives unique descriptions.
- `web/tests/e2e/large-table.nojs.spec.ts` — exactly the two real sort
  links (`source`, `status`), and `/data-freshness/stale/` +
  `/data-freshness/volatility/` return 404.
- `tests/unit/test_p34_11_copy_batch.py` — all batch hashes verify; the
  new pages map and ids bind.
- `tests/unit/test_data_collection_page.py` — `_norm` unfolds `{" "}` like
  the batch test; all DC bindings still verify.
- axe WCAG 2.2 AA sweep covers the four chrome pages (`CHROME_PAGES` in
  `pages.ts` joins `A11Y_PAGES` and `ZERO_JS_PUBLIC_PAGES` — they ship zero
  script like every content page).

≈ 970 changed lines across 42 files (a large share tests + copy rows) —
inside the ≤ 3,000 budget excluding generated files.

## Boundaries / notes

- **No production mutation, no republish.** `live_verification=false`; the
  public effect rides P34.17's republish #1. `ops/web/nginx.conf` is
  untouched — its `error_page 403`/`410` wiring and the true `/terms` 301
  are `D-P34.13-1`, owner P34.40's dark roll.
- **N-6/N-7 verbatim.** The 410 body and the `/terms` notice are the
  ratified notice strings (sha-checked against the planning document);
  every other new public sentence is a `pending` copy-batch row — only
  `confirmed` copy ships, so republish #1 stays gated on the operator's
  verbatim confirmation.
- **Sort semantics unchanged where real.** `source` and `status` still
  sort; stale counts and volatility classes still render as columns. Only
  the affordances that lied were removed — restoring them is UX9-2's.
- **No client JS added.** The chrome pages are `chrome="minimal"` static
  HTML and join `ZERO_JS_PUBLIC_PAGES`; nothing else changed in the
  script budget.
- **Append-only.** DEFERRALS gained one row (`D-P34.13-1`, cites BL-084);
  batch-01 only gained rows; protected records untouched until closeout.
